page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with a running head above it. Below the text: two centred closing lines, then a catchword at the right. A woodcut ornament sits in the lower half of the page, with no text.

main_text.l: super eos. Hoc in ciuili administratione Dominus. Quid in Ecclesiastica ferret nos nobis, ut
regem, sed Deum alterum, tanquam ab ipso datum & constitutum fingentes? qui terras, mare,
coelumque & tartara regat & administret; cui omnia agere ferre licet: qui Reges potestatem legi-
bus leges dare; qui sacra vertere, mutare, pro animi libidine possit? Non ferret, quomodo [illegible,
~12 letters] suum non tulit alienos sibi Deos fingentem. Igitur illi, postquam ita animo collubitum [illegible, ~10
letters] um ne regnet super eos, abiiciant, & Dei verbum ludibrio habeant. Nos Christiani Reipublicæ
cives, Christum Regem, servi Dei, Christum Dominum; corporis Christi membra, Christum
caput unum agnoscamus: datis scriptisque à Deo, tanquam ab auctore, & rege, & Domino nostro,
legibus insistamus; neque nos Rhetorum declamationibus, tanquam ventis circuma-
gi patiamur. Servire Regi Regum Deo, Libertas est. Sed ser-
vis servorum servire, etiam à servitute de-

page.notes: The top line is a fragment that continues from the previous page ("super eos."). A black blotch over the right-hand part of the first lines makes several words illegible: "ferret", "quomodo", "collubitum" and the words after it. Some letters in "ferret" and "possit" are doubtful. The closing motto is in spaced capitals and is read as MORDVR with a doubtful ending. A short mark ("11") sits at the far right edge beside the last line of the text. It is probably a printer's mark or show-through and is not a note. The woodcut ornament is not text and is not transcribed. The catchword IOAN: is at the right below the last printed line.
